clue.text: The regular players are standing firm

parts.note: standing in the sense of permanent or habitual, as a standing joke is a stock joke
a firm is a business company

explanation.surface: A theatre's regular troupe refuses to budge in some dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standing firm' reads as one phrase meaning resolute; it splits into two words each giving half the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stock company is a repertory troupe of actors attached to one theatre who perform a rotating set of plays.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink is for the non-driver

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a cocktail of brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice
second meaning: the passenger car bolted beside a motorcycle

explanation.surface: A drink fit for whoever is not behind the wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the passenger may drink because someone else drives; the second half is literally the seat a motorcycle passenger rides in.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a brandy cocktail and the small passenger carriage attached to the side of a motorbike.

clue.text: Getting over-poetic about marine ear-shell

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece is wrapped around the other

parts.note: o'er is the poetic contraction of over
RM stands for Royal Marine

explanation.surface: Someone waxing lyrical about a seashell.
explanation.walkthrough: Marine is a noun here, a soldier, not the adjective it seems to qualify. An ormer is an abalone, a Channel Islands delicacy whose shell is ear-shaped.
explanation.definitionFit: The ormer is a kind of abalone, also called sea-ear, a mollusc whose flattened shell resembles a human ear.

clue.text: The man who could lay his hands on a fortune!

definitions.text: The man who could lay his hands on a fortune!

parts.words: lay his hands on a fortune
parts.note: surface reading: someone able to get hold of a great deal of money
setter's reading: the legendary figure whose touch turned anything into gold

explanation.walkthrough: To lay hands on something usually means to acquire it; here it is literal, as every object this mythical ruler touched became a fortune in gold.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Phrygian ruler was granted the gift that everything he touched turned to gold.

clue.text: Is responsible for snow-clearance

indicators.note: a clearance clears things out and moves them about, so the word before it gets its letters rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is in charge of clearing snow from the roads.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated snow-clearance looks like one job; it splits into the fodder and the signal that shuffles it.
explanation.definitionFit: To own a problem or task is to accept being accountable for it, as in owning a mistake.

clue.text: Meadows in unsullied environs delight

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the second
environs are surroundings, so the word before it encloses the other piece

parts.note: unsullied means clean, untainted
a lea is a meadow, a favourite crossword word

explanation.surface: Meadows in clean, unspoilt surroundings are a joy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unsullied environs' reads as one description of the meadows' setting; environs here signals that the adjective's word goes round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasure and delight are close synonyms for a feeling of happy satisfaction or enjoyment.

clue.text: An upside-down home fit only for pigs — disgusting

indicators.note: in a down clue upside-down turns the word over so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written, then turned over
a sty is a pigpen

explanation.surface: A messy, ramshackle house only pigs could live in is revolting.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasty means unpleasant or repellent, a direct synonym of disgusting as an adjective.

clue.text: Quip about a top man one can make in company

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes round what follows

parts.note: a sally is a witty retort
OC is Officer Commanding, the man in charge
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A witty remark about the boss that is safe to make at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: The inserted pair goes in after the quip's first letter, not at its middle. 'Company' looks like a business; it means other people's society.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something socially means doing it among other people, in a sociable setting with friends.

clue.text: The way to get in some exercise and acquire a heavenly body

indicators.note: getting in means going inside, so the first piece is placed within the second

parts.note: PT is physical training
a lane is a way or road

explanation.surface: Advice on fitting in a workout to get a beautiful figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavenly body' reads as a toned physique; here it is astronomical.
explanation.definitionFit: Planets orbit stars and are classic examples of celestial objects seen in the night sky.

clue.text: Control gained by, party man with nice manoeuvring

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: manoeuvring means moving things around into new positions

parts.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A politician seizing power through clever manoeuvres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party man' looks like a single political figure, but party gives the opening letters and man joins nice in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominance is power or ascendancy over others, the state of having control.

clue.text: Seat to set in the sun

indicators.note: set in means placed inside, so the first word is put within the other

parts.note: Sol is the Latin name for the sun
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chair put out for sunbathing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' suggests the sun going down, but it is part of the container signal, and the inserted word goes in after the sun's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A stool is a simple backless seat for one person, usually with three or four legs.

clue.text: An element of decoration in front of a capital

definitions.note: chrome is the everyday name for chromium

indicators.note: in front of means the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: CH is Companion of Honour, a British decoration
Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: An ornamental feature on the facade of a city building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An element of decoration' reads as one phrase; it splits at 'of'. CH is a British honour, the Companion of Honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Chrome is a common name for chromium, a metallic chemical element used in shiny plating.

clue.text: Byron's lupine descendent

parts.note: surface reading: some wolfish heir of the poet's family line
setter's reading: the invader who, in a famous Byron poem, comes down like a wolf on the fold

explanation.walkthrough: Byron's 'The Destruction of Sennacherib' opens with this invader who 'came down like the wolf on the fold': lupine means wolflike, and descendent means coming down, not offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: The first line of Byron's poem compares the attacking Mesopotamian army to a wolf descending on sheep.

clue.text: Live in if the fare's ideal

indicators.note: in tells us the letters are found inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: You would stay at a hotel if the food were perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live in' looks like the definition, as to reside is to live in a place; the in is the signal, and the answer hides in fa-RE'S IDE-al.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to live there, to have one's home in that place.

clue.text: Division to give voice about at all times

indicators.note: about means going round, so the first word surrounds what follows

parts.note: to sing is to give voice
ever means always

explanation.surface: A split arising because people keep speaking out all the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Severing is the act of cutting apart, so it can stand for a division or separation.

clue.text: An armband or two permitted

parts.note: a brace is a pair, as of pheasants
let means allowed

explanation.surface: Allowed to wear one armband or a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracelet is an ornamental band or chain worn around the wrist or arm.

clue.text: Many on a train may appear in the pink

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the first piece follows the second

parts.note: a car is a carriage of a railway train
a nation is a great many people

explanation.surface: Lots of train passengers look red-faced or in fine health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the pink' is an idiom for healthy; here the pink is a flower. In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece below the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinks are flowers of the genus Dianthus, and the carnation is the best-known member of that genus.

clue.text: Prospect for gold in Central America

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the second

parts.note: Panama is a country of Central America
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Panning for gold somewhere in Central America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prospect for gold' reads as a verb phrase; prospect is a noun, a wide view. Or is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospect is an extensive view of a landscape, and a panorama is a wide unbroken view.

clue.text: Game seaman, first-class

parts.note: fives is a ball game played with the hand against a wall, like squash, in British schools
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor who is up for anything is top-notch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game seaman' reads as a willing sailor; game is a noun, a sport, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Five-star is the top rating for hotels and restaurants, so it describes the highest quality.

clue.text: Iron man's woman

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a male is a man

explanation.surface: A tough guy's girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is not possessive; it is 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Female as a noun means a woman or girl, the counterpart of a male.

clue.text: Putting a light in the garden sounded asinine

indicators.note: putting something in somewhere places it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a flower bed in a garden
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: Someone talking foolishly about installing a garden lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: Asinine looks like it means silly; here it means donkey-like, literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means of a donkey, and the noise a donkey makes is a bray.

clue.text: Lower price for papers under rising journalist

indicators.note: under in a down clue means placed below, so it comes second
in a down clue rising means the word reads upward, from bottom to top

parts.note: ED is short for editor
the press means the newspapers

explanation.surface: Cutting the cover price of newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: To depress a price or value is to push it down, to make it lower than before.

clue.text: Deface the label attached to a Turk's cap

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or deface
a tag is a label
on as in fixed on

explanation.surface: Vandalising the label stuck to a fez.
explanation.walkthrough: A Turk's cap reads as a fez, but it is the name of a lily with swept-back petals.
explanation.definitionFit: The martagon is a lily whose curled-back petals give it the common name Turk's cap lily.

clue.text: Representative of preservationists seen after a time

indicators.note: seen after means placed following, so the first piece comes second

parts.note: an age is a period of time
NT is the National Trust, the British charity that preserves historic houses and land

explanation.surface: A conservation charity's spokesman arrives after a long wait.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent acts on behalf of someone else, which is exactly what a representative does.

clue.text: Enhanced the appearance? That's not true

definitions.meaning: first meaning: applied cosmetics to the face

explanation.surface: Someone doubts a claim that a look was improved.
explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is an adjective; 'That's not true' stands in for a reply calling a story invented.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both wearing cosmetics and fabricated, as a story invented rather than real.

clue.text: Duel to be arranged — with point or foil

indicators.note: arranged means put in order, so the letters are set out anew

parts.note: taken as written
E for east, one of the compass points

explanation.surface: A sword fight is being set up, with pointed blades or fencing foils.
explanation.walkthrough: Point and foil look like fencing words; point is a compass point joining the shuffle, and foil is a verb, to frustrate or escape.
explanation.definitionFit: To elude is to evade or baffle, as a puzzle eludes a solver, much as to foil is to thwart.

clue.text: City-centre church causing some irritation

indicators.note: centre picks out the middle of the word before it

parts.note: the two middle letters
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A cathedral in the middle of town is a source of annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is a mild irritating sensation, or figuratively a nagging annoyance or craving.

clue.text: He wants clean jumble

indicators.note: a jumble is a muddle, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man asks for tidy secondhand goods, as at a jumble sale.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumble sale is a British charity sale of used goods. 'He' defines a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Lance is a male first name, so a single man called that can be referred to as he.

clue.text: Lay at the door of a property

definitions.meaning: first meaning, a verb: to credit or blame someone for something
second meaning, a noun: a characteristic quality

explanation.surface: Leaving something on a house's doorstep.
explanation.walkthrough: Stressed on the second syllable it is the verb; on the first, the noun. 'Property' reads as real estate but means a quality.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascribe responsibility is to lay a thing at someone's door; a trait or quality is a property.

clue.text: People dependent on public transport

parts.note: surface reading: commuters with no car who must take the bus
setter's reading: dependent means literally hanging, from the loops provided for standing passengers

explanation.walkthrough: Dependent comes from the Latin for hanging down, so these passengers literally hang from overhead loops on a crowded bus or train.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing commuters who cannot find seats hold the hand loops suspended from the carriage ceiling.
